slides.header: Your notch, now an AI command center.
slides.subtitle: Dictation, meetings, screen help and 20+ tools in one Mac app. Private by default. Pay once.
body: SparkV for macOS
Seed round · [TBD: month and year]
sparkv.si
slides.notes: SparkV turns the MacBook notch into a drawer that opens when you hover it: media, a file tray, your day, a converter, knowledge Spaces and a hub of more than 20 agents. The AI runs on the Mac by default, so we pay nothing per user for AI. That is why we can sell it once instead of monthly. In two minutes I will show it working, then the numbers.

slides.header: Mac power users rent five apps for one workflow.
slides.subtitle: Notch, clipboard, dictation, meeting notes and screenshots are sold separately, and the AI ones are subscriptions.
body: $395.99 in year one for five separate apps
$312 a year for AI dictation plus AI meeting notes
Five shortcuts, five windows, five bills
slides.notes: This is the stack a busy Mac user ends up with: a notch app, a clipboard manager, a dictation app, a meeting-notes app and a screenshot tool. Using public list prices, year one costs about $396, and the two AI subscriptions alone are $312 a year, every year. Cloud AI has a cost on every request, and subscriptions are the norm for these tools. We do not have that cost; it is the core of our business model.

slides.header: One drawer. Every tool. Right under the camera.
slides.subtitle: Hover the notch: 12 header buttons, 21 drawer pages and a 22-tile agents hub.
body: Notch core: media, volume and battery, tray, AirDrop, your day
Productivity: clipboard, converter, downloads, search, Spaces
AI: dictation, screen help, reply drafts, meetings, translation
Developer tools: UI Audit, Browser Flows, Flow Canvas
slides.notes: Everything lives in one place the user already looks at. Hover the notch and the drawer opens; move away and it closes. The header has six pages on the left and six actions on the right, and the agents hub launches every tool. When the drawer is closed, live activities such as volume, battery, AirPods, notifications, meetings and recordings show beside the camera. All 21 drawer pages render in the real app layout, and every tile and hotkey is wired.

slides.header: Live demo: 90 seconds, all on the Mac.
slides.subtitle: Talk, ask, record and find, with Groq switched off.
body: Hold fn, speak, release: clean text is typed for you
Hold ⌃⌥ and ask: SparkV answers and points to the spot
One click records a meeting: tasks, decisions, answers
⌥Space finds anything you saw, with cited answers
slides.notes: Run this live on the demo Mac; the film I03 is the backup if the room's Wi-Fi, audio or permissions fail. Order: dictation into TextEdit, the screen assistant in Preview, a short recorded meeting, then Universal Search for 'launch' and the agents hub. Say out loud that Groq is off, so everything is on-device. Do not say SparkV clicks or types through other apps on its own: the assistant points and explains; dictation types where your cursor is. The screen assistant is called Clicky in the app today and may be renamed before launch.

slides.header: Meeting notes without a bot in the call.
slides.subtitle: SparkV records your mic and the call audio, transcribes on device and hands you the follow-ups.
body: Minutes, key points, decisions and your tasks with due days
Suggested answers when someone asks you a question

slides.header: Proof it works: one real UI Audit run.
slides.subtitle: SparkV crawled a test site, found the planted bugs and wrote the fix prompt.
body: Summary written on device by Apple Intelligence
Fix prompt pastes straight into Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot
Runs only on sites you own or may test
slides.notes: This is not a mock-up. SparkV's own UI Audit controller audited a bundled test site with planted issues on 127.0.0.1: six pages, 69 findings, three of them critical and fifteen high. Apple Intelligence wrote the summary on device, and the P button produced a 51,666-character fix prompt covering 60 issues. The runner's self-test passes 48 of 48, including never sending a form to a non-test host and never clicking logout or delete. It needs Node.js on the Mac. Its sibling, Browser Flows, is still in beta: its self-test was not clean on 22 October.

slides.header: Why now: the AI already ships inside the Mac.
slides.subtitle: Apple silicon and Apple's on-device models make private AI with zero cost per request possible.
body: Cloud AI apps pay for every request. SparkV pays $0.
Works offline. Audio and screens stay on the Mac.
Every MacBook Pro since 2021 has a notch to build on.

timeline.what: 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro introduce the notch
Mac Pro moves to M2 Ultra: every Mac is now Apple silicon
Foundation Models framework opens Apple's on-device model to apps, 'without cloud API costs'
SparkV 1.0: notarized direct download [TBD: launch date]

slides.notes: Three things lined up. The notch arrived on the MacBook Pro in 2021. Since mid-2023 every Mac Apple sells runs Apple silicon. And at WWDC 2025 Apple opened its on-device model to developers; in Craig Federighi's words, it runs without cloud API costs and works offline. That turns AI from a per-request cost into a free capability of the hardware. Competitors built on cloud models have to charge monthly. We do not.

slides.header: Five jobs, one app, one price.
slides.subtitle: Each rival owns one job. SparkV covers all five and charges once.
body: Breadth: 20+ tools behind one hover
Pay once: no AI bill to pass on
Private by default: on-device models
slides.notes: Read the matrix by column: every competitor is excellent at one job. Notch apps such as NotchNook are built around media and a file tray, and the free open-source one is not notarized. The AI tools, Wispr Flow, Granola and Raycast Pro, are sold as subscriptions. SparkV is the only one in this set that combines the notch with the AI jobs and charges once. The honest risk: any of them can add features. Our answer is breadth plus integration, because Spaces and Search tie meetings, dictation, clipboard and captures together, and the cost structure lets us stay one-time. Prices are from third-party listings; we re-check them before every send.

slides.header: Free to start. $39 once for everything.
slides.subtitle: Sold direct, with Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record for tax and license keys.
body: Free hooks users away from free notch apps
Pro is one price for every feature
Team adds recurring revenue from companies
slides.notes: Three plans. Free is a useful notch app at zero, which competes with the free open-source option and gives reviewers something to try. Pro is $39 once, $29 in launch week, and includes every feature; buyers on r/macapps prefer one-time prices and CleanShot X shows the model works. Team is $8 per seat per month, billed yearly, minimum three seats, for companies that need invoices, seat management and an MDM package. We are not on the Mac App Store because SparkV needs Accessibility and other APIs the sandbox does not allow; Lemon Squeezy handles VAT, GST and sales tax worldwide. Shared Spaces for Team is a file package today, not live sync.

Optional renewal $19/yr; the app never stops working
Minimum 3 seats; one invoice (PO or bank transfer)

table.footer: 14-day full Pro trial, no card · 50% student discount · 30-day refunds · Alternative held back: five feature packs at $9-19 each (all five = $39)

slides.header: We keep about 94% of every Pro sale.
slides.subtitle: On-device AI means no inference bill. The only variable cost is the payment fee.
body: $0 AI cost per user
$99 a year fixed (Apple Developer); no MoR monthly fee
3 Pro sales cover the fixed Apple fee

table.title: Net per sale by plan (USD)
table.basis: Lemon Squeezy 5% + $0.50 per order; +1.5% non-US; +0.5% on subscriptions (Team). Team row = (3 x $96 - 5.5% - $0.50) / 3.

slides.notes: Our gross margin is the payment fee and nothing else. On a $39 sale Lemon Squeezy takes 5 percent plus 50 cents, so we keep $36.55; about $36 from a non-US buyer. AI runs on the Mac, and the optional Groq path uses the buyer's own key, so inference costs us nothing. Fixed costs are the $99 Apple Developer fee, a domain and static hosting for the site and update feed. The chart on the right is arithmetic, not a forecast: it shows what tiny shares of one year's Mac shipments would be worth. Our real revenue plan is marked TBD until the beta gives us a conversion rate.

slides.header: Go to market: waitlist to Product Hunt in 30 days.
slides.subtitle: Demo-first and creator-led. Affiliates earn 30%, only when a sale happens.
body: Product Hunt, r/macapps App Pile, Show HN
YouTube: one 2-4 min demo plus a 30 s Short per feature
Comparison pages: SparkV vs NotchNook, Alcove, boring.notch

timeline.what: Apple Developer ID, Lemon Squeezy products, domain
Legal pages; Face Unlock out of the sold build
Demo video, 5 Shorts, keys to 10-15 creators
Product Hunt (Tue/Wed), r/macapps, X, LinkedIn, waitlist email

slides.notes: The plan is in the business plan, day by day. Days one to fifteen make the app sellable: Developer ID, notarization, licensing and a clean-Mac test. Then the landing page and waitlist, a demo video and Shorts, keys for creators, a private beta of 30 to 50 users, and launch on a Tuesday or Wednesday on Product Hunt and in the r/macapps App Pile thread. Affiliates are paid only on sales. Setapp is a second channel from month three. The targets on the bottom row are TBD; we will set them from the waitlist and beta numbers.

slides.header: Built and tested. Launch numbers come next.
slides.subtitle: Pre-revenue today. This is what is verified, and what we will report.
body: Full app compiles; every tab, tile and hotkey is wired
50 real views rendered with sample data
Open: Browser Flows self-test not clean; live hardware checks pending
slides.source_line: Internal checks run 22 Oct 2026 against current sources (feature guide, verification summary).
slides.notes: We are pre-revenue and pre-launch, and I will not dress that up. What exists: the full app compiles with the Command Line Tools, every drawer tab, hub tile and default hotkey is wired, 50 views were rendered from the real code, and the automated harnesses pass, about 29,000 widget checks, 195 clipboard checks, 63 OCR and recorder checks and 48 of 48 UI Audit runner tests. What is still open: the Browser Flows self-test was not clean, and features that need a microphone, camera or system permission are on a live-check list before launch. The bottom row is what we will report to you monthly.

After launch: Setapp, packs, Team sync, reliability

slides.notes: Investors should hear the risks from us first. Four things block the first sale and all four are on the 30-day plan: proper Apple signing and notarization, licensing code, the face-recognition model's non-commercial license, which we solve by leaving Face Unlock out of 1.0, and the Node.js dependency of the developer tools. One more risk: SparkV uses private macOS paths for media and the HUD. Fallbacks already exist, and Sparkle lets us ship fixes fast. After launch, the order of Setapp, packs and Team sync is TBD and will follow what beta users ask for.
